issues.description: LLD upgrade() prose specifies 'role VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK(role IN (...))', but the migration uses a PostgreSQL named ENUM type (user_role_enum). The LLD models section for auth.py correctly specifies Enum('STAFF','VERIFIER','SUPERVISOR'), creating an internal contradiction in the LLD. The migration resolves this by following the ORM model (Enum), which is the correct choice per DS-009 (ORM-first). The code comment on lines 17-18 explicitly documents the rationale.
issues.fix_instruction: No fix required — implementation is correct. ORM model auth.py uses sa.Enum with name='user_role_enum'. Migration follows ORM per DS-009. The inaccuracy is in the LLD upgrade() prose description, not in the migration code.
issues.spec_ref: T-074-plan.json scope; LLD file.upgrade.description vs LLD file.functions[UserModel].description

issues.description: tbl_user_master has BOTH a column-level UNIQUE constraint (username column's unique=True, which PostgreSQL implements as a unique B-tree index) AND a separate non-unique index via op.create_index('ix_user_master_username', ...). This is redundant — the unique constraint's backing index already covers the same lookup path. However, the migration correctly mirrors the ORM model's __table_args__ (Index('ix_user_master_username', 'username') coexists with unique=True on the column) per DS-009.
issues.fix_instruction: No fix required in migration — ORM model is the source of truth per DS-009. If redundancy is to be eliminated, the fix belongs in backend/src/infrastructure/db/models/auth.py: remove Index('ix_user_master_username', 'username') from UserModel.__table_args__ and regenerate the migration. That change is out of scope for T-074.
